info.bio: Durante muchos años tras de su aparición, Accept sufrió constantes cambios en su formación, manteniéndose esencialmente en el nivel amateur, haciendo apariciones esporádicas en festivales. Su carrera profesional comienza en 1976, cuando fueron invitados a tocar en uno de los primeros festivales de rock 'n roll en Alemania — Rock am Rhein. Después del festival, la banda recibió la oferta y entró al estudio profesional por primera vez, a fin de grabar su primer disco autotitulado Accept

scenes.name: La edad de oro del heavy metal
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Weinstein divide la historia en cinco eras: erupción (1969-72), primera cristalización (1973-75), edad de oro o cristalización plena (1976-79), crecimiento (1979-83) y fragmentación en subgéneros (desde 1983). El núcleo del género es el código fijado en la edad de oro. Su sonido es poder: volumen, guitarra solista virtuosa con pedales y distorsión, solos obligatorios, bombo y un bajo amplificado que hace «pesado» al heavy y se siente en el pecho, y una voz emocional y potente (los aullidos de Plant y Halford, el tono operístico y áspero de Dio) que compite con la guitarra sin vencerla. En lo visual, logotipos angulosos, portadas negras y rojas con imágenes ominosas, ropa de calle, luego el cuero motero y desde 1980 el spandex. En las letras, dos polos: lo dionisíaco (sexo, alcohol y, sobre todo, el elogio del rock y del volumen) y el caos (diablo, infierno, monstruos, injusticia, locura, suicidio y muerte), con la noche como mediadora entre ambos. Tras la fragmentación sigue vivo como «classic metal», el puente entre lite metal y thrash.

podcast.title: Historical UK Market Presence
podcast.body: Accept was mentioned as one of the few non-American heavy metal and hard rock bands that had a presence in the British market during a long period when American bands dominated. "American metal and hard rock bands pretty much had the British market to themselves, with a couple of bands like Accept and Scorpions thrown in."

xref.title: Pioneering Modern Las Vegas Residency (2003)
xref.body: Celine Dion was one of the first artists to accept a modern Las Vegas residency deal, beginning in 2003. Over the next four years, she significantly redefined the Vegas entertainment scene, attracting audiences not just for gambling but specifically to see her performances. Her success led to a second residency at Caesar's Palace from 2011 to 2019. "Celine Dion was one of the first to accept such a modern deal. This was in 2003."

xref.title: Grammy Awards Acceptance (2014)
xref.body: Even when accepting their Grammy Awards in 2014, they maintained their robot personas, having someone else speak on their behalf. "And even when they appeared on stage to accept their Grammy Awards in 2014, they had someone else do the talking."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tom DeLonge's Departures (2014-2015)
xref.body: Tom DeLonge initially quit the band for one day in early 2014 but was persuaded to return. Tensions escalated again in early 2015 when he insisted on recording his parts in San Diego while Mark and Travis worked in LA. A week before studio convergence, Mark and Travis received an email from Tom's manager stating his unwillingness to participate, citing a desire to focus on non-musical projects. Another account suggests he was presented with a 60-page contract demanding sole focus on Blink, which he couldn't accept due to prior commitments. He consequently quit for a second time. "Tensions built, and a week before everyone was supposed to convene in the studio for the final push, Mark and Travis got an email from Tom's manager saying that he no longer wanted to participate in Blink 182."

xref.title: Band Decision on Licensing
xref.body: Despite their punk rock purist ethos, the $18,000 licensing offer for "Strawberry Fire" was more than the band could make in a year. When Robert and Hillary consulted the rest of the band, there was no hesitation, and the unanimous decision was to accept the money.

xref.title: Dispute Over Ticket Price Split
xref.body: Pearl Jam sought an "all-in" ticket price of $25 but wanted Ticketmaster to reduce its service charge from $4 to $2, which would increase the band's take from $21 to $23 per ticket. Ticketmaster refused this demand, instead suggesting that Pearl Jam could achieve their $25 ticket price if they agreed to accept less for the base price of the ticket. "But then Pearl Jam said, no, no, no, no, you charge $2 so we could make $23 for ticket and ticket master would refuse saying that the band could have their $25 ticket if they agreed to take less."

xref.title: Pioneering Indie-to-Major Transition
xref.body: Husker Dew was among the first indie bands to accept an offer to jump to a major label, a move that initially generated whispers of a "sell-out." However, by sticking to their creative vision, they demonstrated that it was possible to record for a major label while still maintaining an indie attitude. "Husker do had recently done the same thing. At first, there were whispers of sell-out, but both bands stuck to their creative guns."

xref.title: Reclusive Lifestyle
xref.body: Kate Bush spends most of her time at her home in Southeast London, completely out of public view, with her reasons for absence from the spotlight never adequately explained. She made videos under very controlled circumstances. "Most of the time Kate spent at her home in Southeast London, completely out of public view, and say for a very rare interview, and the one or two times she showed up to accept some kind of life-some achievement award, that's been it. But the reasons for her absence from the spotlight have never been adequately explained. She made videos, but under very controlled circumstances."
